review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Preserve exact frontend authentication while separating transient observation gaps and diagnosing bounded startup admission
review.notes: User authorized diagnostics/startup readiness; no real restore or live input. A local frontend handshake currently coalesces missing process/TTY evidence and hard mismatches into 403 without diagnostic reason. Admit only kernel peer tied to this controlled child launch, stable pane/root/client birth and foreground TTY. Wait for cmd.Start identity publication before evaluating an early connection. Use a single 4s admission context, at most 4 attempts and cancellable pauses only for unavailable observations; peer/home/pane/TTY/birth/ambiguity conflicts refuse without retry. Inspect direct child launches with two snapshots of exact pane/bridge/client PIDs; generic launchers retain full ancestry resolution and ambiguity protection. Reuse the existing terminal verifier and legacy Resolve contract, preserve excluded/native modes and no relaunch/fallback after child starts. Emit value-free stage/cause/attempt/timing diagnostics and an actionable local error without prompt/argv/credentials. Record old-red/new-green using isolated deterministic inspector/gate seams; no production daemon, user thread, permissions or installed services. Runtime/real reboot acceptance is separate. Planned source changes may add context-aware inspection and ReadAgent while legacy wrappers retain budgets. Follow-up owner review at frozen 81e800cb: the original active sequence advances before admission/upgrade, so a rejected or pending reconnect can silence the valid incumbent. Keep a separate monotonic issued counter and activate only successful upgraded connections; late older successes must not replace a newer active connection. Add CFR-004 before implementing this delta; original CFR-001..003 objects remain unchanged. Bound WebSocket upgrade by the remainder of the same admission deadline, then clear transport deadlines for a long-lived accepted client. Independent Q review c3e443da found uniqueness loss in exact-PID optimization, missing rows misclassified as conflicts, a synchronous process reader that can outlive parent cancellation, and dial errors masking context reasons. CFR-005/006/007 are reviewed before this correction: remove the reduced process scope and preserve two full-tree snapshots for every launch, keep exact controlled-child ancestry at Begin, classify absent required client rows as unavailable without accepting them, observe real unequal rows as hard conflicts, isolate a process reader in a single buffered-result worker so cancellation returns before a blocked read settles, and classify dial cancellation/deadline before daemon-unavailable. No live restore or stuck process experiment. Existing CFR-001 expectation is explicitly corrected here; its first design remains in prior Git history. Epoch delta CFR-004 remains unchanged. Follow-up accurate S history gate refused retroactively adding CFR005/mutating CFR001 on a file first implemented at Q. Preserve this real rejection and restore the original CFR001 object. Retire the obsolete direct-PID scope test file with explicit mapping rationale, and move every still-valid observation/cancellation assertion plus full-tree CFR005 regressions into readiness_review_test.go under CFR005. This new path is designed here before its first implementation edit; no force push, history/base/gate rewrite or waived checks. The full-tree production S bytes stay unchanged. The old fast-scope assumption is intentionally superseded, not silently counted as passing. Accurate S review still found missing intermediate ancestors classified hard while peer exists, and post-Upgrade cancellation mislabeled deadline. CFR-008/009 are reviewed before correction in new test files. Missing any required launch evidence or missing parent on the peer ancestry path is unavailable, never an accepted identity; observed conflicts stay hard. Post-upgrade classification must check actual parent context before the elapsed deadline. Preserve all prior case objects, migration history and S full-check evidence.

cases.description: Terminal readiness observations retain strict identity and use a bounded exact-launch fast path
cases.setup: Synthetic before/after process records, actual inspector/findClient logic, controlled stdin/pane reads and direct/native versus generic launcher ancestry
cases.action: Resolve valid direct and wrapped clients; vary absent snapshots/stdin, foreground/TTY/peer/birth changes, ambiguous branches and pane metadata; inspect exact PID selection and parent-context cancellation
cases.expected: Only stable unique foreground Codex with verified stdin and exact launch ancestry is accepted. Missing reads classify transient; explicit conflicts classify hard refusal. Direct child snapshots are scoped to pane/bridge/client; generic ancestry keeps existing protections. Cancellation does not extend the parent deadline; legacy Resolve behavior is unchanged. No real process or terminal mutation.

cases.description: Frontend admission reports typed causes and binds only the controlled launch
cases.setup: Actual Begin frontend function with isolated HOME/CODEX_HOME, injected current pane/client observation and process incarnation readers
cases.action: Admit exact launch; vary peer versus client, launch ancestry, backend command/birth availability, invalid request, pane disappearance and canceled inspection; compare persistent files before/after
cases.expected: Known peer/launch mismatch, invalid identity and changed pane cannot acquire authority; transient unreadable evidence is distinguishable from mismatch. No thread discovery/resume/input or persisted binding occurs during admission. Legacy Begin API and current binding/freshness checks remain valid.

cases.description: Bridge waits for launch publication and retries only transient admission within one deadline
cases.setup: Actual readiness/admission driver, controlled attempt and wait functions, real cancellation channels with deterministic ordering and synthetic typed errors
cases.action: Deliver an early request before launch publication, then open the gate; exercise transient-then-ready, mismatch, exhausted attempts, deadline/cancel and launch failure; inspect HTTP/status reason and diagnostic fields
cases.expected: No check executes before publication; successful transient retry authorizes exactly once. Hard refusal runs once, no second child or native fallback, failures preserve specific nonsecret reason and retry eligibility. All attempts share a 4s parent budget and at most four checks; canceled/deadline work cannot later authorize. Old immediate refusal fails the transient/early-publication expectations; cancellation does not require a timing-race sleep.

cases.description: Rejected or out-of-order connection attempts cannot retire a verified active frontend
cases.setup: Actual production connection epoch allocator and activation/current predicates; deterministic reservation/activation order, no sleeps or real sockets
cases.action: Activate A, reserve failed/in-flight B, activate C before late B; try zero, unreserved and repeated activation; inspect incumbent ownership after every step
cases.expected: Reservation does not change active authority. Only a successfully upgraded reserved connection can activate; a failed or older connection cannot suppress incumbent heartbeat/binding. A newer successful connection retires only the prior active epoch. Original pre-admission sequence-guard semantics fail the failed-reservation assertion. One admission deadline includes the WebSocket upgrade; no deadline is retained on the accepted interactive transport.

cases.description: Direct launch cannot bypass ambiguity and partial snapshots never authorize
cases.setup: Actual ObserveLaunch with injected exact/full ps variants, known peer/child and controlled before/after rows; all still-valid strict identity and parent-cancellation assertions retained from the retired CFR001 file
cases.action: Observe direct and generic launches with second eligible foreground client existing or arriving in second snapshot; omit peer in nonempty before/after then restore full observation
cases.expected: Every launch checks full-tree uniqueness. Existing or new eligible sibling refuses without verified PID. Missing peer or ancestor rows yield retryable process-unavailable; a genuinely changed birth remains hard process-changed. No input or authority is granted on incomplete evidence. The old exact-PID path fails the paired sibling counterexample.

cases.description: Process admission reader returns at parent cancellation despite a blocked underlying read
cases.setup: Production ReadAgentContext wrapper and injected reader blocked by deterministic entered/release channels
cases.action: Enter blocked reader, cancel parent, observe return before release, then release worker; compare immediate valid and canceled reads
cases.expected: Caller returns unavailable promptly at cancellation without awaiting underlying reader; a late result cannot authorize or write shared output. Exact process result remains unchanged for timely valid reads. No real hung process or service is created.

cases.description: Daemon dial admission preserves fixed cancellation and deadline diagnostics
cases.setup: Production dial-and-classify helper used by handler, injected failed/successful/canceling dial
cases.action: Return context cancellation, deadline, ordinary dial error and success; inspect actual returned admission reason/status
cases.expected: Context cancellation/deadline take precedence over generic daemon-unavailable; errors returned as context values remain specific even before ctx.Err updates. Ordinary dial failure remains daemon-unavailable and no retry mutation/fallback occurs.

cases.description: A nonempty launch snapshot missing intermediate ancestry remains retryable evidence
cases.setup: Production ObserveLaunch with known pane/bridge/child/peer records and deterministic snapshot sequence, including peer-present missing bridge or unlisted intermediate parent
cases.action: Omit a required or intermediate ancestor in the first read, then restore complete ancestry on the next read; compare real birth/TTY conflict and ambiguous-client counterexamples
cases.expected: Missing rows refuse without client authority and report process-unavailable with retry eligibility. A later complete stable snapshot can succeed within the same parent budget. Genuine observed mismatch or ambiguity remains a hard refusal even when another row is unavailable. No live process or session is used.

cases.description: The actual post-upgrade decision preserves cancellation versus deadline causes
cases.setup: Production completion-classification helper used by the accepted WebSocket handler, controlled canceled/live/expired contexts and future/past deadlines
cases.action: Cancel a parent while its deadline is still future, expire a deadline, and keep a live budget; inspect the exact diagnostic reason used by the production branch
cases.expected: Canceled upgrade records admission-cancelled; exhausted budget records admission-deadline; live completion continues. A rejected completion does not activate the epoch and no HTTP reply is fabricated after upgrade. Existing epoch and identity checks are unchanged.
